title: Predictive error-budget pulse and capacity hedging playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents the predictive error-budget pulse process and the automated/manual capacity hedging patterns Redwood SREs use to avoid SLO burn and graceful-degrade user impact. It combines short-term forecasting, signal thresholds, automated mitigations, and manual escalation steps.

Audience: SREs, on-call engineers, platform owners, and incident commanders for inference services.

Scope: Applies to multi-tenant model-serving routes exposed via Redwood API and Dedicated pools. Targets availability-style and latency P99/P95 SLOs. Not intended for billing or billing-only throttles.

Owner and contacts

- Playbook owner: SRE Capacity & Resilience (eng-sre)
- Primary on-call: inference-sre rotation
- Pager escalation: inference-team@redwood.ai, oncall-phone (see org directory)

Signals and telemetry

We rely on these core signals (priority order):

1) Prometheus metrics (primary)
- service_request_latency_p95, service_request_latency_p99
- request_success_ratio_5m (successes/total)
- token_consumption_rate (tokens/s per pool)
- queued_requests and active_workers per pool

2) Traces & sample logs
- Trace spans over 5s for generation path
- Error types: OOM, OOM-kv, model-cold-start, gpu-timeout

3) Observability derived series (used by forecasting & alerts)
- rolling_error_budget_burn_24h (calculated by SLO pipeline)
- predicted_error_budget_burn_72h (model forecast)
- capacity_headroom_ratio = (available_slots / target_slots)

Forecasting model (short description)

- Purpose: provide a 72-hour probabilistic forecast of error-budget burn and capacity headroom to inform preemptive actions.
- Inputs: 1h/5m telemetry series (latency P99, QPS, tokens/s), scheduled deployments, known maintenance windows, recent model rollouts, anomaly flags, week-of-year, hour-of-day.
- Model type: ensemble (exponential smoothing + gradient boosted tree for exogenous features). Forecast outputs: median and 90th percentile burn-rate and headroom.
- Housekeeping: retrain weekly with latest 6 weeks of data, validate on holdout, alert on >15% model drift.

Policy: thresholds and decision matrix

Table: Decision thresholds (applies per service/route/pool)

| Signal | Action trigger | Primary action | Escalation window | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| predicted_error_budget_burn_72h >= 80% (90p) | imminent risk of SLO violation | start automated hedging pipeline level-1 | 30m | confidence-weight with model output |
| rolling_error_budget_burn_24h >= 50% | early caution | prepare mitigation snapshot, notify PM/owner | 2h | runbook ready |
| capacity_headroom_ratio <= 0.15 | low headroom | throttling + scale-up attempt | 15m | prefer safe scale actions |
| service_request_latency_p99 increase > 50% vs baseline | user-visible latency | degrade non-critical routes, enable lower-quality model variant | 10m | preserve core SLA routes |

Automated hedging pipeline (levels)

Design principles: automated actions must be reversible, safe-by-default, and logged/audited. Each level increases intervention scope. Automation runs in the control plane with circuit-breakers and manual approval gates for disruptive steps.

Level 0 — Observation and notification
- Trigger: rolling_error_budget_burn_24h >= 30% or small predicted bump.
- Actions: create an incident ticket (internal), post to #sre-alerts with summary and forecast link, snapshot routing policies.

Level 1 — Lightweight automated mitigations (non-disruptive)
- Trigger: predicted_error_budget_burn_72h >= 50% (median) OR capacity_headroom_ratio <= 0.25.
- Actions (automated):
  - Enable request batching tweaks: increase max_batch_wait_ms by +20% (safe sample), enable prefix-KV cache for high-hit routes.
  - Increase autoscale target for dedicated pools by +10% (if spare capacity in region).
  - Temporarily prioritize high-value tokens (per-customer weights) if customer tier policy allows.
- Observable endpoints: /ops/hedge/status and automated runbook log.

Level 2 — Moderate automation with controlled degradation
- Trigger: predicted_error_budget_burn_72h >= 80% (90p) OR capacity_headroom_ratio <= 0.10.
- Actions:
  - Swap non-critical routes to cheaper model variant (e.g., fp16 → int8 quantized) with grace period for soft rollbacks.
  - Apply soft-rate-limits to background requests (retry-after headers).
  - Activate cross-region routing fallback to alternate region pools (if latency acceptable).
  - Notify product owners and SRE manager.

Level 3 — Aggressive emergency actions
- Trigger: rolling_error_budget_burn_24h >= 100% OR rapid latency spike causing user-impact.
- Actions:
  - Enforce strict per-tenant throttles for non-critical classes.
  - Initiate emergency scale (spin up reserved burst nodes) using warm image; if unavailable, enable degraded-read-only features for admin tooling.
  - Escalate to incident commander and exec on-call.

Safety and rollback controls

- Every automated change is: idempotent, tagged with correlation-id, and reversible via the control-plane undo API (opsctl hedge rollback <id>).
- Automation is rate-limited (max 1 hedge action per 5 min per-service).
- Post-action canary monitoring runs for 5 minutes verifying latency and error rate improvements; if worse, automation auto-rolls back.

Manual runbook: step-by-step

1) Confirm signals and validate forecast
   - Query latest rolling_error_budget_burn_24h and predicted_error_budget_burn_72h in Grafana.
   - Check recent deploys: kubectl get deployments --namespace=model-serving -l rollout=true --since=24h.

2) If Level 1/2 triggers are met and automation has not started, run automated pipeline from opsctl:
   - opsctl hedge start --service <service> --reason "predictive-pulse" --level 1
   - Watch correlation-id logs: curl -s "https://ops-api/hedge/<id>/status" | jq .

3) For Level 2 manual confirmations (model swaps, route changes):
   - Prepare model-variant config: edit /configs/route-overrides/<route>.yaml and push to canary using gitops (PR + auto-merge allowed for emergency).
   - Promote canary after 10 min of stability.

4) For Level 3 emergency steps:
   - Page the incident commander and request exec on-call.
   - If cold-starts or OOMs are primary cause, remove offending rollout: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> --namespace=model-serving
   - If capacity insufficient, trigger reserved-burst: opsctl capacity reserve --pool <pool> --nodes 4 --reason "emergency-hedge"

Communication templates

- Slack incident header (use #sre-alerts):
  HEADING: [HEDGE] <service> predicted error budget burn >= <threshold> – automatic mitigation applied (level X)
  BODY: Summary, actions taken, current telemetry links, expected next check-in in 15 minutes.

- Customer-facing/Ticket note (for status page):
  "We are mitigating increased delays for <service>. We have applied prioritization and are working to restore standard performance. No data loss expected. Status updates every 30 minutes."

Operational tooling and queries (appendix)

- Key Grafana dashboards: SRE > Predictive SLO Pulse, Service Headroom, Hedging Actions Audit.
- Example Prometheus query (rolling 24h error budget burn):
  sum_over_time((1 - request_success_ratio_5m)[24h:5m]) / count_over_time(requests_total[24h:5m]) * 100

- Example BigQuery forecast job (pseudocode):
  SELECT service, forecast_median, forecast_p90 FROM inference_forecasts WHERE run_ts = CURRENT_DATE() - 1

- opsctl sequence examples:
  - Start hedge: opsctl hedge start --service inference-api --level 1 --comment "auto-run"
  - Rollback: opsctl hedge rollback --id <correlation-id>

KPIs and post-action validation

- Short-term KPIs (0–2h): reduce predicted 72h burn to <50% at 90p or restore headroom >20%
- Medium-term KPIs (2–24h): rolling_error_budget_burn_24h decreases by >=30% vs peak
- Validation steps: confirm P95/P99 improvement, confirm no increase in customer 5xx rate, verify canary and rollback logs.

Incident review & continuous improvement

- Every predictive pulse that results in a Level 2+ automated mitigation must have a post-action review within 3 business days. Review template:
  - Timeline, root cause (infrastructure, model, traffic shift), forecast accuracy, automation decisions and whether rollback was needed, suggested config fixes, owner for follow-up.
- Track what threshold values triggered actions and tune decision thresholds quarterly.

Runbook exercises and validation

- Quarterly simulations: run a synthetic forecast spike in staging that triggers Level 1 and 2 flows. Check that automation actions respect safety gates and that rollback flow works end-to-end.
- Metrics to monitor during exercises: automation success rate, false positives (automation triggered incorrectly), time-to-stable-state.

Appendix A — Configuration reference (examples)

| Config key | Default | Allowed range | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| hedge.max_automations_per_hour | 6 | 0-20 | throttle for hedge automation events |
| hedge.scale_inc_pct | 10% | 0-50% | percent increase applied to autoscale targets |
| hedge.batch_wait_ms_delta | 0 | -50% to +200% | delta applied to batching latency budget |

Appendix B — Troubleshooting quick hits

- If automation fails to scale up: check capacity provider logs (cloud-provider), verify quota. Command: cloudcli quotas describe --region <r>
- If model-swap causes quality regressions: revert variant and create a prompt-set smoke test: evals run --suite quick-quality-check --service <service>

Ownership and next steps

- Maintainers: SRE Capacity & Resilience (primary), Runtime Team (secondary for model-variant ops).
- Roadmap items: integrate short-term demand forecasting into routing controller (Q2 2026), add drift alerts to forecast pipeline, add customer-aware hedging policies.
